items.title: 2.10 Inelastic collision in one dimension (ek dimension mein inelastic takkar) (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of topic 2.10 with Fig. 2.16 and Example 2.10 (PDF 45-46, 50; printed 42-43, 47).

blocks.text: Do bodies lein jin ke mass m₁ aur m₂ hain aur jo ek hi line mein v⃗₁i aur v⃗₂i velocities se chal rahi hain, aur v⃗₁i > v⃗₂i (peechhe wali tez hai). Is case mein m₁ ko projectile aur m₂ ko target kehte hain. Kuch time (t) baad dono inelastic collision karti hain aur aapas mein chipak jati hain. Ab un ka combined (mila hua) mass m₁ + m₂ hai jo collision ke baad final velocity v⃗f se chalta hai (Fig. 2.16).

blocks.alt: Collision se pehle: ball m1 velocity v1i se aur bari ball m2 velocity v2i se, dono right taraf. Collision ke baad: ek bari body m1 + m2, andar dark hissa, velocity vf se right taraf.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.16: One dimension mein perfectly inelastic collision (kitab ki Figure 2.16 ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing).

blocks.text: Collision perfectly inelastic hai, phir bhi total momentum conserved rehta hai. Law of conservation of momentum se:

blocks.latex: \text{Total momentum of system before collision} = \text{Total momentum of the system after collision}
blocks.text_alt: Total momentum of system before collision = Total momentum of the system after collision

blocks.text: Yeh collision ke baad mili hui body ki common (dono ki ek hi) velocity hai.
Special case: agar target m₂ ruka hua ho (v₂i = 0) to equation yeh ban jati hai:
Yani m₁ ki velocity mass ratio m₁/(m₁ + m₂) ke hisaab se kam ho jati hai. m₁ ka mass jitna zyada ho, combination (mili hui body) utni tez chalti hai.
Ab kinetic energy dekhte hain. Collision se pehle system ki kinetic energy:
Collision ke baad mili hui body ki kinetic energy:
Inelastic collision mein kinetic energy ka jo fraction (hissa) lost hota hai:
Eq. (2.37) se vf ki value rakhein:

blocks.text_alt: ((K.E)i - (K.E)f)/(K.E)i = ([½m₁v₁i² + ½m₂v₂i²] - ½(m₁ + m₂)[m₁/(m₁ + m₂)]² v₁i²) / [½m₁v₁i² + ½m₂v₂i²]

blocks.text: Ab special case lein jab target m₂ ruka hua ho (v₂i = 0). Solve karne se:

Yeh inelastic collision mein lost hone wali kinetic energy ka fraction hai. Is se saaf hai ke one dimension ke inelastic collision mein energy lost hoti hai. Example: m₁ = m₂ ho to aadhi kinetic energy lost ho jati hai.

blocks.title: Example 2.10
blocks.problem: 2 kg mass ki projectile 4 m s⁻¹ ki initial velocity se right taraf chal kar 3 kg ke ruke hue target se takrati hai. Collision ke baad dono chipak kar ek body ki tarah 1.6 m s⁻¹ se chalte hain. Momentum ka conservation aur energy loss (nuqsan) dikhayein. (Kitab mein yeh example topic 2.12 ke baad chhapa hai.)
steps: Pehle ka momentum (x-direction): pₓ = m₁v₁ₓ + m₂v₂ₓ = (2 kg × 4 m s⁻¹) + (3 kg × 0) = 8 kg m s⁻¹
Combined mass M = 2 kg + 3 kg = 5 kg, final velocity 1.6 m s⁻¹
Baad ka momentum: M vf = 5 kg × 1.6 m s⁻¹ = 8 kg m s⁻¹, yani momentum conserved hai
Pehle ki K.E. = ½ × 2 kg × (4 m s⁻¹)² + ½ × 3 kg × 0 = 16 J
Baad ki K.E. = ½ × 5 kg × (1.6 m s⁻¹)² = 6.4 J
blocks.answer: Momentum conserved hai lekin 9.6 J kinetic energy lost hui. Yeh one dimension ka perfectly inelastic collision hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab is example ko "perfectly inelastic collision in 2D" kehti hai. Lekin dono bodies collision se pehle aur baad ek hi straight line (x-direction) mein chalti hain, is liye yeh one dimension (1D) ka collision hai, 2D ka nahi.

blocks.caption: Perfectly inelastic collision (one dimension)
rows: vf = 1.6 m s⁻¹; K.E. 16 J se 6.4 J, yani 9.6 J lost (3/5 = 60%)

blocks.prompt: Example 2.10 ke answers equations (2.37) aur (2.38) se check karein.
blocks.explanation: vf = m₁v₁i/(m₁ + m₂) = 2 × 4/5 = 1.6 m s⁻¹, jaisa diya gaya hai. Lost fraction m₂/(m₁ + m₂) = 3/5 = 0.6 hona chahiye, aur waqai 9.6 J / 16 J = 0.6.

items: Perfectly inelastic: bodies chipak jati hain; momentum conserved: m₁v₁i + m₂v₂i = (m₁ + m₂)vf; target ruka hua ho to vf = m₁v₁i/(m₁ + m₂) aur lost K.E. ka fraction m₂/(m₁ + m₂). Example 2.10: momentum pehle aur baad 8 kg m s⁻¹, 16 J mein se 9.6 J lost.
